title: Post-incident follow-up: per-tenant cgroup caps, reservation recalibration, and soft-burst throttles
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: After the capacity event on 2025-02-12 where tenant A's training workload caused widespread eviction and latency SLO breaches for multi-tenant Dedicated clusters, we need a set of actionable follow-ups to reduce blast radius for noisy tenants, fix reservation mis-sizing heuristics, and introduce a soft-burst throttling mechanism. This ticket coordinates implementation, testing, and rollout for the three-pronged mitigation and ensures required observability and runbook updates.
background: What happened: a large multi-hour job with an unbounded token generation pattern exhausted GPU memory and compute on several nodes. Autoscaling did not absorb the load due to reservation fragmentation and cold-start constraints. Existing burst policy allowed short, unthrottled bursts that amplified contention. Impact: multiple customers experienced elevated latency and evictions; incident postmortem linked below.
goals: 1) Contain noisy tenants with per-tenant cgroup limits and a lightweight isolation path. 2) Recalibrate reservation sizing algorithm to avoid overcommit and under-provision scenarios. 3) Implement soft-burst throttles that maintain latency SLOs while allowing graceful short bursts. 4) Add telemetry and alerts to prevent recurrence and speed diagnosis.
acceptance_criteria:
- Node-level and tenant-level cgroup enforcement is in place for Dedicated clusters and does not break existing workloads.
- Reservation recalibration algorithm uses 7d p95 + safety factor and has A/B experiment demonstrating reduced eviction rate by >=50% in synthetic noisy tests.
- Soft-burst token-bucket implemented with configurable tokens per tenant and recovery rate; integration tests show latency SLOs (p99 < configured target) under bursty traffic.
- Dashboards updated and a new alert fires when burst-token consumption exceeds 80% for 2 minutes.
- Playbook updated and validated by oncall through a tabletop exercise.
- Changes rolled out via canary to 5% of clusters, then 25%, then 100% with rollback automation in place.
technical_design_notes:
- Isolation: use Linux cgroup v2 to enforce per-tenant GPU memory 'soft' caps plus discrete scheduling priority (SCHED_BATCH -> SCHED_DEFAULT demotion for noisy processes). Implement as an option in the node agent to avoid control-plane churn.
- Reservation recalibration: change heuristic from '30-day average' to '7-day p95 with 1.25 safety multiplier' for reservation size suggestions. Persist historical per-tenant seq-len distribution to object store and sample at 6h intervals.
- Soft-burst: token-bucket implemented at node-agent and request-router. Each tenant receives tokens proportional to reservation size; tokens consumed per token-generation request based on expected token delta. When tokens exhausted, requests are queued with progressive backoff rather than immediate eviction.
- Fallbacks: if queueing latency > 200ms for a tenant tier with SLA, automatically route to a lower-cost model variant or fallback region if policy allows.
- Metrics: add tenant.burst.tokens_used, tenant.cgroup_triggers, reservation.recalibrate_events, eviction.count_by_tenant.

testing_plan:
- Unit tests for token accounting and cgroup enforcement.
- Integration test that launches 50 synthetic tenants with one noisy tenant generating sustained high token rates; measure eviction rate and latency. Goal: eviction rate drop >=50% vs baseline.
- Canary on non-prod Dedicated cluster with traffic mirroring for 48h.
- Chaos run: kill a node and verify reservation recalibration prevents mass eviction.
- Oncall tabletop to run through playbook and verify alerts and runbook steps are actionable.
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flags behind 'tenant_isolation_v1' and 'soft_burst_v1'. 2) Canary to internal clusters (5%) for 48h, monitor tenant.burst.tokens_used and eviction.count_by_tenant. 3) Increase to 25% for 72h with extended monitoring. 4) Full rollout after sign-off. 5) Migration window for reservation recalibration: run in advisory mode for 14 days, send recommended reservation sizes to customers, then auto-apply after 30 days unless opted out.
observability_and_alerting:
- New dashboards: 'Dedicated > Tenant Isolation', 'Reservation Recalibration Health', 'Soft Burst Consumption' with p50/p95/p99 latency broken down by tenant.
- Alerts: 'tenant_burst_token_high' (>=80% tokens for 2m), 'cgroup_throttle_rate_high' (>5% of pods throttled in 5m), 'eviction_spike' (evictions > baseline * 3 in 10m).
- Pager runbook: immediate mitigation: reduce noisy tenant reservation, attach dedicated pool, enable temporary hard cgroup limit.
notes:
- Migration rationale: 7d p95 captures recent shifts in workload patterns for fast-moving customers and reduces both under- and over-provisioning.
- Risk: aggressive cgroup caps could affect long-tail LLM decoding behavior; mitigation: start as soft caps with telemetry then tighten.
- Cost: token-bucket queuing may increase tail latency and slightly increase infra cost due to longer job lifetimes; expected net reduction in eviction cost and reduced customer impact.
